set.pl: 20-acre farm, S part of W½ SE¼ sec. 27 T1N R6W (Bellevue Twp), about 1 mi east of Bellevue; Battle Creek River about ¼ mi north (1913 Eaton County atlas)
pinev: Parcel-level: 1913 Standard Atlas of Eaton County shows the 20-acre farm in the S part of the W½ SE¼ sec. 27 T1N R6W (about 200 m).
set.st: Feb 1914: two strangers from Bay City dug up two or three old stumps on this farm and left on the first train, and Bellevue went treasure mad. A year earlier a self-styled detective had shown county officials a map of an iron safe with about $15,000, said stolen from a county treasurer's office in the 1850s and buried near the river by four men. The theft is unverified and the strangers may have taken whatever was there. Private farmland: permission.
set.t: The strangers may have taken it. Access: private farmland, ask permission.
src: Standard Atlas of Eaton County, Michigan (1913)
